Mister Maxinomics, you’ve made a beautiful and genuinely instructive video, but I think the conclusion is fundamentally wrong. Stop comparing AI to technologies of the past. The analogy simply breaks down. AI is not merely another productivity tool replacing one category of human labor with another. It is increasingly capable of performing cognitive tasks themselves—and in many domains, it is already outperforming humans. We are also approaching something qualitatively different: recursive AI-driven improvement. Once we have genuine AGI—not the watered-down definition currently marketed by OpenAI—the economic implications become difficult to compare with any previous technological revolution. And if AGI arrives within the next few months, as I believe it might, the question won't be whether companies *prefer* humans. It will be whether there is any rational economic reason to hire a human for a task that an AI agent can perform 100 times better, at a fraction of the cost, continuously, and at massive scale. At that point, comparing AI to the Industrial Revolution, the internet, or any previous technology isn't just inadequate. It fundamentally misses the nature of the transition we may be entering.
